public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 897

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
- [Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
- [ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
- [Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function.
  Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
- [Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth.
  Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos897

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The answer is no; this follows from a construction of Wirsing [Wi81], rediscovered by
Archivara [Ar25] and formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean"]
theorem erdos_897.parts.i : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/ f(n) = ∞$?

The answer is no; the same counterexample is formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean"]
theorem erdos_897.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Wirsing [Wi70] proved that if $|f(n+1)−f(n)| ≤ C$ then $f(n) = c \log n + O(1)$ for some constant
$c$. This is Erdős Problem 491; see `erdos_491`, whose linked formal proof gives this statement.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos491.lean#L34"]
theorem erdos_897.variants.log_growth
    (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (C : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ n, |f (n+1) - f n| ≤ C) :
    ∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ n, f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n := by
  sorry


/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/f(n) = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos897

findings.description: The conclusion is `∃ c, ∃ O, O =O[atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ n, f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n`. That is only a one-sided bound: f(n) − c·log n is eventually bounded above. Wirsing's theorem, stated in the docstring and in `erdos_491`, is two-sided: f(n) = c log n + O(1). The one-sided claim is elementary and does not need Wirsing. Additivity with 2 gives f(2n) ≤ f(2) + f(n) + 3C for every n ≥ 1: split on the parity of n, and when n is even use n+1, which is coprime to 2. Strong induction then gives f(m) ≤ (|f 2| + 4C)·log m / log 2. I proved this in Lean (`theorem log_growth_elementary`, ~60 lines, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only) and checked `example : type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.log_growth := log_growth_elementary`. So the declaration tagged `research solved` with a formal proof of Wirsing's theorem states a much weaker claim than the result it cites.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/897 (LaTeX source): "Wirsing \cite{Wi70} proved (see [491]) that if $\lvert f(n+1)-f(n)\rvert \leq C$ then $f(n)=c\log n+O(1)$ for some constant $c$." The repository's `erdos_491` states `(fun n ↦ f n - c * Real.log n) =O[atTop] (fun _ ↦ 1)`. The linked plby Erdos491.lean proves `|f n - c * log n| ≤ 2M`, i.e. a two-sided bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `≤` with `=`: `∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ n, f n = c * Real.log n + O n`. Equivalently use `∃ c : ℝ, (fun n : ℕ ↦ f n - c * Real.log n) =O[Filter.atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ))`, matching `erdos_491`.

findings.description: The disjunct meant to encode Erdős's strongly additive case, `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p`, also quantifies over k = 0, which gives f 1 = f p. Additivity with a = b = 1 forces f 1 = 0, so f p = 0 for every prime and f(p^k) = f p = 0 for every k. The limsup hypothesis is then ≤ 0 ≠ ⊤. The strongly additive alternative therefore contradicts the other hypotheses, and the theorem only covers completely additive f. Proved in Lean: (a) additivity plus this disjunct implies the file's limsup is `≠ ⊤`; (b) the variant's right-hand side is `↔` to the same statement with only the disjunct `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p`. The source's special case f(p^k) = f(p), which Tao says is still open, is lost. If a strongly additive counterexample existed but no completely additive one, the Lean answer would be True while the source's answer would be False.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/897: "Erdős suggested that for simplicity one might first assume that $f(p^k)=f(p)$ or $f(p^k)=kf(p)$." Forum thread 897, Tao: "this is a different model from either of the two models f(p^k)=f(p), f(p^k)=kf(p) proposed by Erdos, for which the conjecture may well still be true." Here p^k is a prime power, so k ≥ 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the strongly additive disjunct to positive exponents: `(∀ k p, p.Prime → 0 < k → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = k * f p) → ...`. Better still, split it into separate theorems for the strongly and completely additive cases. The fixed disjunct is satisfiable, e.g. f(n) = Σ_{p∣n} p·log p.

findings.description: This has the same hypotheses as `variants.parts.i`, so it has the same defect. `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p` at k = 0 gives f p = f 1 = 0 for all primes, so f vanishes on prime powers and the limsup hypothesis cannot equal ⊤. I proved in Lean that this disjunct plus additivity makes the limsup `≠ ⊤`. The ratio question for strongly additive f, one of Erdős's two suggested special cases, is therefore dropped; only the completely additive case is posed.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/897: "Or perhaps even $\limsup_n f(n+1)/f(n)=\infty$?" and "Erdős suggested that for simplicity one might first assume that $f(p^k)=f(p)$ or $f(p^k)=kf(p)$."
findings.suggested_fix: Use `(∀ k p, p.Prime → 0 < k → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = k * f p)`, or state the two special cases as separate theorems.

findings.description: All four theorems read $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k)/\log p^k = \infty$ as a limsup along `Filter.atTop ⊓ 𝓟 {(p,k) | p.Prime}` on `ℕ × ℕ`. `atTop` on `ℕ × ℕ` is the product filter `atTop ×ˢ atTop` (checked: `prod_atTop_atTop_eq`). The hypothesis therefore requires f(p^k)/log p^k to be unbounded on every corner {p ≥ N, k ≥ N}, with both the prime and the exponent tending to infinity. The source's limsup ranges over prime powers p^k → ∞. The Lean hypothesis is strictly stronger. In Lean I built F(n) = Σ_{p ∈ n.primeFactors} (if n.factorization p = 1 then p·log p else 0) and proved: F is additive; F(p^k)/log p^k is unbounded above on prime powers (F(p)/log p = p); yet the file's limsup is ≤ 0, because F(p^k) = 0 for k ≥ 2. No truth value in the file changes. For parts.i/ii (`answer(False)`) the Lean asserts a stronger 'no', which is still true because the Wirsing/Archivara f(q) = g(q) log q satisfies both readings and the formal proof checks the stronger one. For the variants, the strongly/completely additive hypothesis makes the two readings equivalent. Still, the right-hand side of parts.i/ii is not the source's proposition.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/897: "\limsup_{p,k}\frac{f(p^k)}{\log p^k}=\infty". Archivara paper, Lemma 1 proof: "Since log* q → ∞ along any sequence q → ∞ (for instance along q = 2^m as m → ∞), the limsup over prime powers is infinite." That path has p fixed at 2, which the product filter ignores.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the limsup over prime powers, e.g. `(Filter.cofinite ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime ∧ 0 < k}).limsup (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤`. Alternatively use `(Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {q : ℕ | IsPrimePow q}).limsup (fun q => (f q / Real.log q : EReal)) = ⊤`.

review.notes:
Lean scratch files are in /workspace/review/: vac.lean (variants), loggrowth.lean (log_growth), prodfilter.lean (product filter). All compile with only standard axioms.

What I checked and found faithful:
- parts.i and parts.ii use `answer(False)`, which matches the source ("The answer to both questions is no"). The linked plby proof proves exactly these statements. Their `research solved` tags match erdosproblems.com (DISPROVED (LEAN)).
- The variants' `research open` tag matches the source: Erdős's suggested special cases, which Tao says "may well still be true". No status issues.

Minor points, not reported as findings:
- The ratio f(n+1)/f(n) uses EReal division, where x/0 = 0. For "limsup = ⊤" this is the same as ignoring n with f(n) = 0, and the known counterexample has f(n) > 0 eventually.
- The module docstring does not cite the original source [Er72, p.85].
- The parts.i docstring is missing a closing parenthesis.
- The `formal_proof` link on log_growth points to a proof of the stronger two-sided statement, so it remains valid after the suggested fix.

demonstrated.claim: The lemma `strongly_additive_clause_kills_limsup` proves that the clause `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p` (k = 0 included) plus additivity makes the limsup hypothesis `≠ ⊤`, hence `type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i` is proved equivalent to the same statement with only the completely additive clause (a supporting example shows ω, the standard strongly additive function, fails the clause at k = 0), so Erdős's strongly additive case is vacuous.

By the same lemma, `type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.ii` is proved equivalent to the same statement with only the completely additive clause, so the strongly additive case of the ratio question is vacuous.

The file's conclusion formula `∃ c O, O =O[atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ n, f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n`, instantiated at f n = −n, holds with c = 0 and O = 0, while the two-sided form `(fun n ↦ f n − c·log n) =O[atTop] 1` (Wirsing's theorem, as in `erdos_491`) is proved false for −n for every c, so the Lean conclusion is only a one-sided bound.

submission.summary:
`/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` contains the following.

- **Open variants (`variants.parts.i` and `variants.parts.ii`).** An 8-line lemma shows that the clause `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p` quantifies over k = 0 as well. So it forces f p = f 1 = 0 for every prime, and then the limsup hypothesis cannot equal ⊤. Using the lemma, each variant is proved (named via `type_of%`) equivalent to the same statement with only the completely additive clause. The strongly additive case f(p^k) = f(p) is therefore lost. A one-line supporting example shows that ω (number of distinct prime factors) fails the clause at k = 0.
- **`log_growth`.** One example copies the conclusion with f n := −n: it holds with c = 0 and O = 0. A second example proves that the two-sided form of Wirsing's theorem fails for −n, for every c. Together they show the conclusion is only an upper bound. A full elementary proof of the declaration as stated (the doubling argument, about 60 lines) is in `/workspace/review/loggrowth.lean` and type-checks against `type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.log_growth`. I left it out of this file because it is not a few-line check.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«897»

/-! Demonstrations for Erdős 897. Note: `answer(sorry)` elaborates to `True`, so the type of each
open variant is `True ↔ ...`. -/

open Filter

/-- With `k = 0` allowed, the clause `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p` gives `f p = f 1 = 0` for
every prime `p` (additivity at `a = b = 1` forces `f 1 = 0`). So `f` vanishes on prime powers and
the variants' limsup hypothesis cannot hold. -/
theorem strongly_additive_clause_kills_limsup (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (h1 : ∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) :
    (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) ≠ ⊤ := by
  have h0 : ∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = 0 := fun k p hp => by
    have e1 := hf 1 one_pos 1 one_pos (Nat.coprime_one_left 1)
    have e2 := h1 0 p hp
    simp only [mul_one, pow_zero] at e1 e2
    linarith [h1 k p hp]
  refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top EReal.zero_ne_top (limsup_le_of_le (by isBoundedDefault) ?_)
  refine mem_inf_of_right (mem_principal.2 ?_)
  rintro ⟨p, k⟩ (hp : p.Prime)
  simp [h0 k p hp]

-- Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i: the statement is equivalent to the same statement with
-- the strongly additive alternative `f (p^k) = f p` deleted. That alternative is unsatisfiable
-- (lemma above), so only completely additive `f` are covered and Erdős's case f(p^k) = f(p)
-- is lost.
example : type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i ↔ (True ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) :=
  iff_congr Iff.rfl ⟨fun h f hf hL hC => h f hf hL (Or.inr hC), fun h f hf hL hor =>
    hor.elim (fun h1 => absurd hL (strongly_additive_clause_kills_limsup f hf h1)) (h f hf hL)⟩

-- Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.ii: same defect. The statement is equivalent to the same
-- statement with only the completely additive alternative.
example : type_of% @Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.ii ↔ (True ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤) :=
  iff_congr Iff.rfl ⟨fun h f hf hL hC => h f hf hL (Or.inr hC), fun h f hf hL hor =>
    hor.elim (fun h1 => absurd hL (strongly_additive_clause_kills_limsup f hf h1)) (h f hf hL)⟩

-- Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i and parts.ii (supporting check): ω(n) = #(prime factors),
-- the textbook strongly additive function (ω(p^k) = ω(p) = 1 for k ≥ 1), fails the variants'
-- clause `f (p^k) = f p` at k = 0, because ω(1) = 0 ≠ 1 = ω(2).
example : ¬ ∀ k p, p.Prime →
    (fun n : ℕ => (n.primeFactors.card : ℝ)) (p^k) = (fun n : ℕ => (n.primeFactors.card : ℝ)) p := by
  intro h
  simpa using h 0 2 Nat.prime_two

-- Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.log_growth: the conclusion is only an upper bound. Its formula,
-- copied with `f n := -n`, holds with c = 0, O = 0 ...
example : ∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ n, (fun n : ℕ => -(n : ℝ)) n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n :=
  ⟨0, 0, Asymptotics.isBigO_zero _ _, fun n => by simp⟩

-- ... whereas Wirsing's two-sided f(n) = c·log n + O(1) (the form in `erdos_491`) fails for
-- -n for every c.
example (c : ℝ) :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ => -(n : ℝ) - c * Real.log n) =O[atTop] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := by
  intro h
  have hn : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) atTop atTop := tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
  have h1 : (fun _ : ℕ => (1 : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) :=
    (Asymptotics.isLittleO_one_left_iff ℝ).2 (by simpa using hn)
  have h2 := (Real.isLittleO_log_id_atTop.comp_tendsto hn).const_mul_left c
  have h3 : (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) :=
    ((h.trans_isLittleO h1).add h2).neg_left.congr_left (fun n => by simp)
  exact Asymptotics.isLittleO_irrefl (hn.eventually_ne_atTop 0).frequently h3

not_fixed.reason: Not fixed: this was reported as 'questionable', and the rules say to leave those alone unless the fix is trivial and safe. The issue is that `atTop` on `ℕ × ℕ` is the product filter, so the Lean hypothesis is stronger than the source's limsup over prime powers. Changing it would alter the solved statements parts.i/parts.ii, whose linked Aristotle proof was checked against the current form. It changes no truth value in the file.

submission.summary:
I edited only FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean (5 insertions, 3 deletions).

(1) `erdos_897.variants.log_growth`: the conclusion is now `∀ n, f n = c*Real.log n + O n` instead of `≤`. This is Wirsing's two-sided f(n) = c log n + O(1), as the docstring and `erdos_491` say.

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 897

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
- [Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
- [ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
- [Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function.
  Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
- [Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth.
  Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).
-/

@[expose] public section
-- TODO(lezeau): add `ArithmeticFunction.IsAdditive` to `ForMathlib`

namespace Erdos897

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The answer is no; this follows from a construction of Wirsing [Wi81], rediscovered by
Archivara [Ar25] and formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean"]
theorem erdos_897.parts.i : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/ f(n) = ∞$?

The answer is no; the same counterexample is formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean"]
theorem erdos_897.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Wirsing [Wi70] proved that if $|f(n+1)−f(n)| ≤ C$ then $f(n) = c \log n + O(1)$ for some constant
$c$. This is Erdős Problem 491; see `erdos_491`, whose linked formal proof gives this statement.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos491.lean#L34"]
theorem erdos_897.variants.log_growth
    (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (C : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ n, |f (n+1) - f n| ≤ C) :
    ∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ n, f n = c*Real.log n + O n := by
  sorry


/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → 0 < k → f (p^k) = f p) ∨
      (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/f(n) = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → 0 < k → f (p^k) = f p) ∨
      (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos897
